question: Should OpenClaw Core own a durable Pi/Review/git-promotion orchestration subsystem and its vendored contracts artifact, or should this workflow remain in the service/plugin owner boundary?
rationale: The patch creates a durable cross-service product boundary rather than repairing an established OpenClaw contract, and repository policy reserves owner-specific runtime behavior for the appropriate plugin or owner repository.

options.title: Keep it outside Core
options.body: Move the orchestration and service-specific contracts to the owning service/plugin repository, exposing only a generic Core seam if one is demonstrably missing.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded Core seam
options.body: Document the intended Core contract and owner, then narrow this PR to a generic supported integration boundary with self-contained tests and an approved dependency model.

options.title: Adopt the full Core subsystem
options.body: Explicitly approve Core ownership of the durable coordinator and assign review across TaskFlow, dependency/security, and service-owner boundaries.

recommendation.title: Keep it outside Core
recommendation.body: Move the orchestration and service-specific contracts to the owning service/plugin repository, exposing only a generic Core seam if one is demonstrably missing.

likelyOwner.reason: No current-main owner could be established from the supplied history; a maintainer with ownership of TaskFlow and Core architecture should make the boundary decision.
